newsitem.title: USA: USDA bars Sun-Diamond from fed purchase programs.
newsitem.headline: USDA bars Sun-Diamond from fed purchase programs.

text.p: The U.S. Agriculture Department on Monday formalized a three-year bar of Sun-Diamond Growers of California from participating in all federal food purchase programs for three years.
In October, USDA proposed barring the fruit cooperative because of its criminal conviction in September for giving illegal gifts to a former Clinton cabinet member.
Sun-Diamond, based in Pleasanton, Calif., had 30 days to appeal.
USDA's Agricultural Marketing Service (AMS) said the action was being taken after a review of information and arguments that Sun-Diamond submitted against the proposed debarment.

"Although AMS is encouraged that Sun-Diamond has implemented a business ethics code, not enough time has elapsed since its implementation in November to establish a safisfactory record that the firms' business practices are protective of the government's interests," it said in a statement.

The USDA said it might consider reducing the ban, which is effective as of October 4, the day it was proposed, "once sufficient evidence exists that Sun-Diamond has rehabilitated its business integrity and honesty.

Sun Diamond was convicted this fall in a federal court on eight criminal counts that included illegal gratuities to former Agriculture Secretary Mike Espy in 1993 and 1994 and illegal campaign contributions to Espy's brother Henry.

The charges arose out of the government's two-year special investigation of the former Agriculture Secretary, who resigned in 1994 amid accusations he took illegal gifts and favors from companies the department regulated.

Earlier this month, USDA also proposed barring the affiliates of Sun-Diamond, who rank as the nation's largest raisin, prune, walnut, fig and apricot cooperatives, from selling to the government. The affiliates have said they would appeal the proposal.
